extracted.intended_audience: general public, member states, partners, investors, and potential IFAD project partners/project designers
extracted.subtask_description: High-level institutional priorities and programmatic principles IFAD expects projects and partners to align with — covering mission, working approach, thematic action areas, governance and results-orientation. Useful for applicants, partners, and project designers seeking IFAD support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investing in rural people
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply put, IFAD invests in rural people. We do this by financing programmes, measuring results, innovating and working with rural people themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should place rural people at the centre, enabling them to take charge of their future and produce nutritious food for their communities; emphasis on long-lasting change by supporting people-led development.

rubrics_metrics.name: People-centred development
rubrics_metrics.description: A core working approach: development must be centred on people (rural producers and communities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes should prioritise empowerment and participation of rural people in design and implementation so outcomes are owned and sustained by communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing for results
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on financing programmes and measuring results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should include clear results frameworks, monitoring and evaluation arrangements (e.g., Results Management Framework, PRISMA dashboard) to demonstrate impact and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transforming food systems
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD’s goal includes transforming agriculture, rural economies and food systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should contribute to systemic change in food systems rather than only isolated interventions, with scalable and sustainable approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting transformative policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Work includes engaging with governments and stakeholders to support policy change that benefits rural people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that include policy dialogue or reforms that enable broader, sustained impacts are aligned with IFAD priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embracing innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD emphasises innovation as part of how it works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should incorporate innovative approaches, technologies or financing mechanisms where appropriate, to increase effectiveness and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting South-South and Triangular Cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD supports cooperation among developing countries and triangular partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that incorporate knowledge exchange, technical cooperation or financing arrangements among countries (South–South/triangular) are favoured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to high transparency and governance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD uses Member State contributions to catalyse additional finance and adheres to the highest transparency and governance standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project design and financial arrangements should meet strong transparency, governance and accountability expectations; institutional safeguards and clear fiduciary arrangements are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalysing funds for greater impact
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD uses contributions from Member States to generate and assemble additional finance for rural people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that leverage IFAD funding to attract co-financing, private investment or blended finance to amplify impact are consistent with IFAD’s model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic targeting: working where needs are deepest
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD works across five regions and in 92 countries, focusing where poverty and hunger are deepest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate geographic targeting to areas of high rural poverty and vulnerability; alignment with regional priorities is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and assessed impact
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD assesses impact and contributes to the SDGs; delivering on mission is emphasised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proposals should articulate clear links to SDG targets and include mechanisms for impact assessment and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic action areas and sectoral priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD’s action areas include empowering rural people (rural women, rural youth, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities), protecting the environment (climate and environment, biodiversity), enhancing livelihoods and markets (private sector, rural finance, markets and value chains, managing land and its resources, promoting sustainable farming, water, crops, livestock, fisheries and aquaculture), and building resilience (rural institutions & organisations, remittances, nutrition, fragile contexts and crises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should align with one or more of these thematic priorities; applicants should show how interventions address specific sub-themes (e.g., gender, youth, climate, markets, land management, nutrition, fragile contexts) and tailor activities accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD works with a broad ecosystem of partners — from foundations to farmers' organisations — to ensure scalable impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that include credible partnerships (local organisations, governments, private sector, civil society) and clear roles for partners are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership, advocacy and visibility for rural people
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD leadership and President play advocacy roles to ensure rural people’s contributions are recognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that incorporate advocacy, knowledge dissemination, and activities that elevate rural voices and evidence can strengthen broader impact and scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge, data and capacity outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD produces research, reports, position papers, practical tools and e-learning as part of its knowledge agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project components that generate evidence, learning products, tools or capacity-building materials — and plans for dissemination — align with IFAD’s emphasis on knowledge and data.
